<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = \ln x</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">dv = dx</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">du = \frac{1}{x}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v = x</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\ln x - \int x \cdot \frac{1}{x}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>x</mi><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= x\ln x - x + C</annotation></semantics></math>.

Finding <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v</annotation></semantics></math> would mean solving the original integral first, so nothing is gained.
